items.title: DQ-first gate policy is a must-be quality
items.summary: QEG must keep DQ precedence, verdict priority, and conditional_go exit code policy unambiguous for IPO-controlled use.
claims: conditional_go is exit code 2 in ipo_controlled

metadata.original_text: IPO controlled Gate policy fixes DQ-first precedence, verdict priority, waiver limits, and conditional_go exit code 2.
risks: If DQ priority is ambiguous, waiver or CI success can invalidate the control model.
metadata.suggested_action: Maintain as hard gate. Map directly to TypeScript types, JSON Schema, evaluator tests, and negative fixtures.

items.title: QEG verdict and human release approval separation is must-be
items.summary: QEG must not synthesize human release approval; approval evidence remains a distinct artifact with authority, role, package hash, and policy refs.
claims: QEG verdict is separated from release approval
ApprovalEvidence requires approver authority and package hash

metadata.original_text: QEG verdict and human release approval are separate controls, and approval evidence must be independently auditable.
risks: If QEG verdict is mistaken for release approval, IPO control evidence becomes invalid.
metadata.suggested_action: Maintain as hard gate and fixture mandatory invalid cases for missing or conflicting approval evidence.

items.title: Evidence package completeness is performance quality
items.summary: The more complete and hash-linked the evidence package is, the more release confidence and audit efficiency improve.
claims: EvidencePackage links inputs, outputs, policy, waiver, approval evidence, manual evidence, and retention evidence
Package phase prevents pre-release artifacts from being used as release Go evidence

metadata.original_text: EvidencePackage must make release judgment reproducible through artifact hashes, phase, policy refs, manual evidence, approval evidence, and retention evidence.
risks: Package contract can be specified but still fail in implementation if hash and phase validation are incomplete.
metadata.suggested_action: Treat as threshold gate. Implement package schema and phase fixtures before any release Go.

items.title: Retention and tamper evidence are must-be for IPO control
items.summary: Silent overwrite and missing retention evidence directly break release traceability, especially for DQ-16.
claims: Storage classification and tamper evidence are release criteria
Retention metadata is required for release evidence

metadata.original_text: Retention, storage classification, tamper evidence, and silent overwrite detection are mandatory release control inputs.
risks: If tamper evidence is only documentary and not evaluated, DQ-16 will be weak.
metadata.suggested_action: Maintain as hard gate. Add storage and overwrite negative fixtures in TASK-10.

items.title: manual-bb plus code-to-gate evidence is attractive but now strategic
items.summary: Combining manual-bb-test-harness with code-to-gate makes the requirement gate unusually strong and differentiating, while not replacing release approval.
claims: manual-bb-test-harness provides risk and black-box gate structure
code-to-gate provides repository static gate evidence
Both are explicitly separated from IPO release approval

metadata.original_text: The pre-implementation Gate combines manual-bb-test-harness and code-to-gate evidence while preserving IPO release No-Go separation.
risks: Differentiating evidence can be overclaimed as release approval if the boundary is not repeated.
metadata.suggested_action: Keep as differentiator. Continue to label code-to-gate passed as static gate evidence only.
